title: Modular eval-runner adapters and stochastic prompt-variant pipeline for reproducible profile publishing
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Problem: Model performance profiles are brittle to small prompt/dataset perturbations and eval-runner differences, which makes pinning model versions unreliable for production rollouts. Goal: Deliver a modular eval-runner adapter layer and a deterministic yet stochastic prompt-variant pipeline that together produce stable, auditable profile artifacts (profile-v2) suitable for version pinning and publishing to the model catalog.

Scope: 1) Eval-runner adapter API that normalizes runner inputs/outputs, captures meta-trace (timings, token counts, hardware tag), and supports runner-specific shims. 2) Prompt-variantizer: a pipeline that creates controlled prompt perturbations (temperature seeds, paraphrases, tokenization-aware truncation, prefix/suffix variants) with deterministic seeding for reproducibility. 3) Dataset shard signer: canonicalize and sign dataset shards used for a profile so profiles can be reproduced and validated. 4) Profile artifact schema v2 that includes the variantization seed map, runner-adapter metadata, and aggregate stability metrics.

Out-of-scope: Changes to model training, core runtime kernel optimizations, or public SDK ergonomics (those will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Eval-runner adapter interface (python) merged and documented, with 3 example adapters: llama-cpp, triton-http, hosted-api
Prompt-variantizer produces N deterministic variants given a seed and config; unit tests covering seeding behavior
Profile-v2 artifacts emitted by harness include variant-seed map, dataset shard signature, and runner meta-trace

End-to-end run on two internal models produces profile artifacts that validate via the shard signature and reproduce within +/- 2% for median latency and +/- 0.5% for token-level perplexity across 5 repeats
Perf dashboard updated to surface profile stability metrics and variant breakdowns
design_notes:
Adapter API: a minimal contract - initialize(config), load_model_meta(), run(batch, options)-> {outputs, meta_trace}. Meta-trace should include per-step timings, kv-cache hits, token counts, and hardware_device_tag. Adapters must expose canonical tokenization and a deterministic batching path. The variantizer is a staged pipeline: (1) canonicalize prompt (normalize whitespace, Unicode NFC), (2) generate paraphrases via lightweight transformer or lexicon rules (configurable), (3) apply token-aware truncation policies, (4) mass-insert benign suffix/prefix variants (controlled probability). All randomness is derived from a single top-level 64-bit seed and per-stage derivations, stored in the profile artifact. Dataset shard signer: compute canonical digest per shard (sorted examples, stable serialization), sign with CI-provisioned signing key (or test-only digest). Profile-v2 stores checksums and a provenance block mapping seeds->variant descriptors.

Trade-offs: Adding adapters increases harness complexity but reduces runner drift. Paraphrase variantization helps surface sensitivity but may increase profile generation time; defaults are conservative (N=8 variants per prompt).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge adapter interface and implement 3 reference adapters behind a feature flag. 2) Land a beta variantizer with N=2 default; run internal smoke profiles on nightly model-onboarding jobs. 3) Iterate on variant policies after 2 weeks of telemetry; increase N to 8 for final profile-v2 generation. 4) Publish profile-v2 to the model catalog and mark old profiles as legacy. 5) Communicate to Integrations and Console teams for UI changes and compatibility notes.
